title: Passive Voice in Action
description: Identify and practice active versus passive voice structures used in news reports, science, and history.

thumbnail.alt: A vintage printing press stamping ink onto a newspaper page
thumbnail.prompt: A vintage printing press stamping ink onto a newspaper page aspect ratio 16:10

questions.prompt: Choose the correct passive form of: "Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928."

options.text: Penicillin was discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928.
Penicillin had discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928.
Penicillin is discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928.
Penicillin was discovering by Alexander Fleming in 1928.

questions.explanation: Past simple passive uses was/were + past participle (was discovered).

questions.prompt: Which sentence is written in the passive voice?

options.text: The suspension bridge was designed by a world-renowned engineer.
A world-renowned engineer designed the suspension bridge.
The engineer is currently designing the new bridge.
Workers finished constructing the bridge ahead of schedule.

questions.explanation: "Was designed by" puts the focus on the bridge rather than the engineer who performed the action.

questions.prompt: Complete the historical fact: "The Mona Lisa ___ from the Louvre museum in 1911 and recovered two years later."
questions.explanation: Because the theft happened at a specific past time (1911), we use the past simple passive: was stolen.

questions.prompt: Why do journalists and news broadcasts frequently use the passive voice?

options.text: To focus on the event itself when the agent is unknown, obvious, or less important.
Because active voice is grammatically forbidden in headline news.
To make written articles informal and humorous.
Because passive sentences are always shorter than active sentences.

questions.explanation: Passive voice is useful when the action or receiver of the action is the main focus of interest.

questions.explanation: For an action completed before another past event, use past perfect passive: had been + past participle.
